### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.snippets

### Question

Howdy. I couldn't figure out if there's a way to do this through reading the docs.

Assume the following snippets:
```
return {
  ["Method"] = { prefix = "method", body = "..." },
  ["Implements"] = { prefix = "implements", body = "..." },
}
```

With the default `mini.snippets` match rules, the sequence `'met'` triggers a match against both of these snippets, since the letters `'m'`, `'e'`, and `'t'` are present in both in that order.

I would like to, if possible, configure the fuzzy matcher to match against the start of the prefix rather than a 'contains' check.

So:
- `'met'` matches the trigger `'method'`
- `'met'` does not match the trigger `'implements'` since `imp` and `met` are different

I checked the documentation for `MiniSnippets.default_match` and the documentation for `matchfuzzy()` but I wasn't able to figure out if this rule can be configured this way.

Thanks!

comment_data.body:
> I would like to, if possible, configure the fuzzy matcher to match against the start of the prefix rather than a 'contains' check.

If I understand correctly, what is described here is not quite "fuzzy matching". The fuzzy matching is "match contains the query/needle in its order, maybe with gaps". So `met` query can fuzzy match even "xxmxxexxt".

The "match against the start" is a strict variant of substring matching. As in `met` will match only `met`, `metx`, `metxx`, etc., but not `xmet`.

> I checked the documentation for `MiniSnippets.default_match` and the documentation for `matchfuzzy()` but I wasn't able to figure out if this rule can be configured this way.

Yeah, `default_match` only matches either exactly (and chooses best exact match if any) or fuzzily (as described above). The substring match requires manual implementation of `config.expand.match`. I'd suggest something along these lines:

```lua
local match = function(snips)
  -- Match based on the word to the left of the cursor
  local line = vim.api.nvim_get_current_line()
  local cur_pos = vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)
  local word_before_cursor = line:sub(1, cur_pos[2]):match('%S*$')

  -- Return all snippets if after whitespace
  if word_before_cursor == '' then return snips end

  -- Try best exact match first
  local exact_match = MiniSnippets.default_match(snips, { pattern_fuzzy = '' })
  if #exact_match > 0 then return exact_match end

  -- Return all snippets that match exactly the start of prefix
  -- All of them will have the same `region` that needs to be replaced
  local res = {}
  local lnum, col, word_width = cur_pos[1], cur_pos[2], word_before_cursor:len()
  local region = { from = { line = lnum, col = col - word_width + 1 }, to = { line = lnum, col = col } }
  for _, s in ipairs(snips) do
    if vim.startswith(s.prefix, word_before_cursor) then
      local new_s = vim.deepcopy(s)
      new_s.region = vim.deepcopy(region)
      table.insert(res, new_s)
    end
  end
  return res
end

local snippets = require('mini.snippets')
snippets.setup({
  snippets = {
    -- Configured snippets
  },
  expand = { match = match },
})
```
